I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize cycle this year. In Quzhou, that is the cropping pattern I know best, and at my age I will choose the most steady and familiar way rather than something that needs too much labor or brings too much market risk. The winter wheat is already in the field at the start of the season, so I will manage it through spring with topdressing, one or two irrigations depending on moisture, and a few pesticide sprays only if I see disease or aphids. After wheat harvest, I will sow summer maize right away so I do not lose soil moisture or the season. I will use improved seed because I want stable yield and stronger resistance, but I will keep fertilizer and water at moderate levels to control cost. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage before maize because it is easier for me than deep ploughing, while the wheat field follows the usual prepared land from last autumn. I am choosing a simple, reliable annual plan that matches local weather, my experience, and the amount of work I can still manage myself.
